doc.title: Arturo Sandoval interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 12, 2023

title: Multi-track Facebook video 'Gracias Republica Dominicana'
summary: Rowe asks about a recent video in which Sandoval plays several parts; he describes the limits of the app and smiling at his own playing.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: I’d like to start out with something quite current. I’ve been watching your FaceBook channel for a while and I took note of a delightful recent song of yours that you put up and I’ll see if I can — it’s called “Gracias Republica Dominicana.”
It’s one of them. There’s hundreds of them.
So I found it really fascinating, for one thing there’s like I don’t know six or seven or eight of you on the screen at the same time.

Yeah. It’s a little application that I’ve been using. It’s very limited, very hard because you cannot punch in, you cannot edit anything, you cannot tune anything, you know whatever you do is what it is. If you don’t like what you did you have to rewind and start from scratch again.
Well that kind of makes you a little more aware of what you’re playing, doesn’t it? It’s like —

Yes. But there was a moment in that, for our listeners I hope they go and check it out because you’ve got like four or five horn parts going on and I liked it when you were improvising because you literally in the other screens were listening to yourself. And you looked happy about it.
Yeah you know sometimes when I like what the other guy did I smile. If I don’t like it I say oh oh.
